Subject: No-model-improvement guarantee + evidence request

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement sign-off, Legal has asked us to confirm two operational guarantees before we finalize the DPA addendum: (1) a firm commitment that MedTech AI customer data will not be used to improve or retrain models (no-model-improvement / no-train), and (2) a practical description of how you will provide proof that our prompts/responses are excluded from model improvement.

High level asks from our side:
- A short ops playbook describing request routing, KV/prefix caching, and how you prevent tenant data from entering training pipelines.
- Evidence options: audit logs, KMS key residency attestations, and sample export of a retention-proof (delete/ephemeral) flow.
- Clarify whether prompt/response ownership (IP) can be contractually asserted or whether only derivative rights are limited.

We'd appreciate something we can send to procurement/legal this week.

Best,
Sonia
Director, Product Security
MedTech AI

Hi Sonia — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-draft ops playbook (redwood-optout-playbook-v1.pdf) and an SFTP/KMS mapping sheet we typically share with regulated customers (sftp-onshore-mapping.xlsx). Quick summary here so your procurement/legal can triage: 

1) No-model-improvement commitment:
- We will include a contractual 'no-model-improvement' clause scoped to customer data submitted to inference endpoints (DPA addendum language available).
- Operationally, we tag tenant traffic at the ingress layer and maintain a policy-controlled routing rule that prevents tagged data from entering any training or continuous fine-tuning pipeline.

2) Evidence & provenance options we can provide:
- Audit trail showing "no-train" tag propagation (retention 1 year by default, extended on request).
- KMS key residency and envelope key logs showing onshore usage for on-prem/KMS customers.
- Exportable CSV of trace IDs for a sampling window (we can produce a proof package you can cross-check).

3) Prompt/response ownership:
- Redwood's standard approach is to grant customers output licensing (non-exclusive) with explicit options in the addendum to assert ownership of prompts and generated outputs for their tenant. Legal will need to agree on language tailored to IP policies (see kimberly's note below).

Next steps: Kimberly can propose redlines for the addendum; Marissa will outline the operational handoff for onboarding; Ben can surface procurement timing/options. If helpful we can schedule a 30-min run-through this week.

— Jonas
VP, Customer Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Hi Sonia — looping in a few clarifying points from Legal to make sure the evidence we provide satisfies procurement: 

1) Scope of no-model-improvement: is MedTech asking for an absolute prohibition (no use for any internal or external research) or an operational exclusion for production inference pipelines only? Absolute prohibitions are possible but carry implications (e.g., inability to run platform-level safety or quality monitoring on aggregated telemetry).

2) Evidence format: we can provide (a) signed attestation with log extracts; (b) a hashed list of trace IDs with corresponding timestamp ranges (so you can independently verify the exported artifacts) or (c) a third-party SOC2 control mapping + supporting logs. Which is most persuasive to your procurement team?

3) Prompt/response IP: Redwood can grant explicit assignment or exclusive licensing of generated outputs to customers in the addendum, but assignment of IP in prompts authored by customer users should be scoped. If MedTech wants assignment for all outputs, we will propose language that limits Redwood's rights to internal telemetry and platform operation.

If you can confirm (1) scope preference, and (2) preferred evidence type, I'll prepare redline language for the DPA addendum and a short checklist your team can use during onboarding.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
